```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(RdistNN)
```

## Overview

`diagnostics()` gives a compact table for fitted DNN-localized estimators. The
method is intentionally fit-object based:

- it uses retained weights rather than refitting;
- it uses retained distances only when `dx` was requested;
- it uses hidden estimator state for NP, CATE, and PLQR diagnostics;
- it marks unavailable diagnostics explicitly instead of reconstructing missing
  inputs from assumptions.

The general fields are available for `np_result`, `cate_result`, and
`plqr_result` objects when weights are retained:

- `n_eff`, `max_weight`, and top-weight shares;
- realized rank radii and weighted distance summaries when `dx` is retained;
- tuning metadata when a tuning spec was used.

Estimator-specific fields are added by the corresponding method:

- NP: weighted outcome mean, standard deviation, and outcome quantiles;
- CATE: treated/control mass and propensity summaries;
- PLQR: residual-regressor Gram eigenvalues and condition number.

Diagnostics require `W`. The default `return = "W"` keeps it. If a fit was
created without weights, refit with `return` including `"W"`.

## Nonparametric Regression

```{r np}
demo_np <- np_demo_data(n = 120, p = 2, design = "sinusoidal", seed = 1)

fit_np <- np_dnn(
  data = demo_np$data,
  x_cols = c("X1", "X2"),
  y_col = "Y",
  x0 = demo_np$x0,
  method = "exact",
  k = 1L,
  s = 4L,
  se = FALSE,
  return = c("W", "dx", "ess")
)

d_np <- diagnostics(fit_np)
d_np[, c(
  "target_id",
  "n_eff",
  "weighted_mean_y",
  "weighted_sd_y",
  "weighted_y_q50"
)]
```

For NP fits, `weighted_mean_y` equals the local mean estimate when the weights
are normalized.

## CATE Overlap

```{r cate}
demo_cate <- cate_demo_data(n = 150, p = 2, design = "hetero", seed = 2)

fit_cate <- cate_dnn(
  data = demo_cate$data,
  x_cols = c("X1", "X2"),
  y_col = "Y",
  t_col = "D",
  m_col = "m_oracle",
  e_col = "e_oracle",
  x0 = demo_cate$x0,
  method = "exact",
  k = 1L,
  s = 4L,
  se = FALSE,
  return = c("W", "dx", "psi", "nuisance")
)

d_cate <- diagnostics(fit_cate)
d_cate[, c(
  "target_id",
  "n_eff",
  "treated_mass",
  "control_mass",
  "treated_share",
  "weighted_mean_propensity"
)]
```

Overlap diagnostics are available when the fit was constructed from treatment
and propensity inputs. If `cate_dnn()` was called with only a direct
`pseudo_outcome`, overlap fields remain present but are marked unavailable.

## Experimental PLQR conditioning

All PLQR functionality, including these diagnostics and its specialized plots,
is experimental and outside the CATE and regression focus of this release.

```{r plqr, eval=FALSE}
demo_plqr <- plqr_demo_data(n = 160, p = 2, p_d = 2, tau = 0.5, seed = 3)

fit_plqr <- plqr_dnn(
  data = demo_plqr$data,
  x_cols = c("X1", "X2"),
  D_cols = c("D1", "D2"),
  g_col = "g_oracle",
  mD_cols = c("mD1", "mD2"),
  y_col = "Y",
  density_col = "density_oracle",
  theta_eval = demo_plqr$truth$theta_true,
  tau = 0.5,
  x0 = demo_plqr$x0,
  method = "exact",
  k = 1L,
  s = 4L,
  se = TRUE,
  return = c("W", "dx", "score", "ess")
)

d_plqr <- diagnostics(fit_plqr)
d_plqr[, c(
  "target_id",
  "n_eff",
  "gram_min_eig",
  "gram_condition_number",
  "jacobian_min_singular_value",
  "jacobian_condition_number",
  "theta_vcov_available"
)]
```

The PLQR Gram diagnostic is based on the localized residual-regressor matrix
`D - m_D(X)`. It is an identification and conditioning diagnostic, not a local
bread estimate.

## Tuning Metadata

When a fit uses `tuning = ...`, the diagnostics table exposes compact tuning
metadata without duplicating the full candidate grid into every row.

```{r tuning}
fit_tuned <- np_dnn(
  data = demo_np$data,
  x_cols = c("X1", "X2"),
  y_col = "Y",
  x0 = demo_np$x0,
  method = "exact",
  k = 1L,
  tuning = tuning_dnn_paper(lambda = 1.25),
  se = FALSE,
  return = c("W", "tuning")
)

d_tuned <- diagnostics(fit_tuned)
d_tuned[, c(
  "target_id",
  "tuning_name",
  "tuning_default_s",
  "tuning_grid_n_candidates",
  "tuning_lambda_default"
)]

attr(d_tuned, "tuning_grid")
```

Use `attr(d_tuned, "tuning_grid")` when you need the full candidate table.

## Availability Rules

Diagnostics avoid hidden recomputation.

- If `W` is missing, `diagnostics()` errors and asks for a refit with weights.
- If `dx` is missing, distance fields are returned as `NA` with
  `distance_diagnostics_available = FALSE`.
- If CATE treatment/propensity state is unavailable, overlap fields are present
  but marked unavailable.
- If PLQR residual-regressor state is unavailable, Gram fields are present but
  marked unavailable.

This behavior keeps diagnostics predictable and prevents the diagnostics layer
from silently rerunning expensive estimator construction.
